summary: Post-#366 PhysicsLabRuntime mining found a representation-transaction contract gap: TransitionObserver is invoked before WorldEntity/Fidelity authorities commit, and callback failure correctly rolls back internal authorities, but the API exposes neither an explicit prepare-only contract nor a post-authority commit/rollback phase. A real F3/F4 adapter that mutates physical representation inside the observer can therefore leave Workspace representation changed even when it subsequently throws and both domain authorities remain at the old fidelity.
evidence: PR #366 exact source builds a WorldEntity preview, invokes observer(current, preview, reason), and only afterward calls registry.transitionRegistered(); FidelityManager commits its own transition only after the hook returns successfully.

#366 regressions prove observer/capture exceptions clear the hidden transitionInFlight guard and preserve registry/Fidelity authority, but they intentionally assert only internal authority/population state; the runtime has no mechanism to undo arbitrary external side effects already performed by the observer.

Docs/PHYSICS_LAB.md names a measured F3/F4 representation/promotion adapter with state capture on demotion as upcoming Reality-Grade work. The current callback shape is therefore directly on the future physical-authority path rather than a generic hypothetical API.

No existing runtime lane/event/PR was found for representation-side commit/rollback acknowledgment. Recommended prerequisite before real F3/F4 promotion: define a narrow transactional adapter contract (for example explicit prepare + commit/rollback semantics, or formally make the precommit callback side-effect-free and provide a postcommit phase) with pure adversarial tests showing an adapter failure cannot leave representation truth ahead of domain truth. Do not implement physical F3/F4 breadth in the finding lane itself.
